title: Equivariant relative coordinate lifts through a Cohen presentation
statement:
Let $C$ be a Cohen ring of residue characteristic $p>0$, with residue field $k$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring], and let $R=C[[t_1,\ldots,t_d]]$ for $d\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $H$ be a finite abelian group of order $N$ invertible in $C$. Suppose $C$ contains a unit $\zeta$ with $\zeta^N=1$ and $1-\zeta^a$ invertible for $1\leq a<N$. Let $H$ act continuously on $R$, fixing $C$ pointwise and satisfying $h(t_i)=\chi_i(h)t_i$ for characters $\chi_i:H\to\langle\zeta\rangle$. Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a complete Noetherian regular local ring with residue field identified with $k$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], [def-weil-regular-scheme], let $H$ act on $A$ by local ring automorphisms, and let $f:R\twoheadrightarrow A$ be an $H$-equivariant local ring homomorphism inducing this residue identification. Assume $z_i=f(t_i)$ form a regular system of parameters of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Let $z'_1,\ldots,z'_d$ be another regular system of parameters with $h(z'_i)=\chi'_i(h)z'_i$ for characters $\chi'_i:H\to\langle\zeta\rangle$, and suppose $z'_i=z_i$ for $1\leq i\leq l$, where $0\leq l\leq d$. Character values on $A$ mean their images under $C\to A$.

There are $t'_1,\ldots,t'_d\in(t_1,\ldots,t_d)R$ with $f(t'_i)=z'_i$, $t'_i=t_i$ for $i\leq l$, and $h(t'_i)=\chi'_i(h)t'_i$. The list $p,t'_1,\ldots,t'_d$ is a regular system of parameters of $R$. The continuous substitution homomorphism $C[[s_1,\ldots,s_d]]\to R$, $s_i\mapsto t'_i$, is a $C$-algebra isomorphism and is $H$-equivariant when $h(s_i)=\chi'_i(h)s_i$. Empty lists and $l=d$ are allowed.

source.place: VIII Lemma 5.5.2, proof, printed p.128, second eigenparameter lifts; relative coordinate condition made explicit using Stacks more-algebra.tex Tag 07NM (lemma-quotient-power-series-ring-over-Cohen), clause (3).

proof.text: Put $I=(t_1,\ldots,t_d)$ and $\mathfrak n=(p)+I$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete], $R$ is complete Noetherian regular local, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$, residue field $k$ and dimension $d+1$. By [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters], $\mathfrak m=(z_1,\ldots,z_d)=(z'_1,\ldots,z'_d)$ and $\dim A=d$. Since $A$ is regular local, [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] gives $\dim_k\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2=\dim A=d$. Thus both parameter lists give bases of that vector space: they span it and each has exactly $d$ members. In particular each $z_i$ has nonzero class when its index exists.

For $i\leq l$, the eigenvector equations for $z'_i=z_i$ imply $(\chi_i(h)-\chi'_i(h))z_i=0$. Two distinct elements of $\langle\zeta\rangle$ differ by a unit: their difference is a unit multiple of $1-\zeta^a$ for some $1\leq a<N$. Its image in $A$ is a unit. The nonzero class of $z_i$ from Step 1 therefore forces $\chi_i(h)=\chi'_i(h)$ in $C$. Set $t'_i=t_i$ for these indices. For $i>l$, write $z'_i=\sum_j a_{ij}z_j$, lift each $a_{ij}$ to $r_{ij}\in R$ using surjectivity of $f$, and put $u_i=\sum_j r_{ij}t_j$. Then $u_i\in I$ and $f(u_i)=z'_i$. This choice, rather than an arbitrary lift in $R$, gives the required zero constant term.

source.place: VIII Lemma 5.5.2, printed p.128, common parameters and choice of lifts, with the variables-ideal condition expanded

proof.text: For $i>l$ define $t'_i=N^{-1}\sum_{h\in H}\chi'_i(h)^{-1}h(u_i)$. The ideal $I$ is $H$-stable since $h(t_j)=\chi_j(h)t_j$, so $t'_i\in I$. Equivariance of $f$ gives $f(t'_i)=N^{-1}\sum_h\chi'_i(h)^{-1}\chi'_i(h)z'_i=z'_i$. For $g\in H$ reindex by $q=gh$; since $H$ fixes $C$ and $\chi'_i(g^{-1}q)^{-1}=\chi'_i(g)\chi'_i(q)^{-1}$, this gives $g(t'_i)=\chi'_i(g)t'_i$. For $i\leq l$ the same eigenvector equation follows from Step 2 and the original action on $t_i$. The argument is a finite-sum identity, requiring no diagonalization or assertion about exactness of invariants.

source.place: VIII Lemma 5.5.2, printed p.128, weighted H-averaging (using the primed character of the vector being lifted)

proof.text: Coefficientwise expansion in [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] identifies $W=I/(pI+I^2)$ with $k^d$, by the coefficients of the degree-one monomials $t_j$. Indeed series in $I$ have zero constant term, terms of degree at least two belong to $I^2$, and the remaining linear coefficients vanish in $k$ exactly when they are divisible by $p$. The map $f$ induces a surjection $W\to\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$: it sends $[t_j]$ to $[z_j]$, kills $pI+I^2$ because $f(p)\in\mathfrak m$, and induces the given residue identification. Step 1 makes it an isomorphism between $d$-dimensional spaces. Therefore $[t'_i]$ form a basis of $W$. Since $pI+I^2\subset\mathfrak n^2$ and $\mathfrak n=(p)+I$, the classes of $p,t'_1,\ldots,t'_d$ span $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] to the finite $R$-module $\mathfrak n$, generated by $p,t_1,\ldots,t_d$: the new list generates $\mathfrak n$. Its length $d+1$ equals $\dim R$ by Step 1, so [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters] says it is a regular system of parameters.

source.place: Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), generator form; ILO VIII 5.5.2, printed p.128, verification that the averaged lifts are parameters

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-full-coordinates-cohen] to the regular parameter system just proved, with coefficient parameter $p$. It gives a $C$-algebra isomorphism $e:C[[s_1,\ldots,s_d]]\to R$ sending $s_i$ to $t'_i$. A ring isomorphism between local rings carries their unique maximal ideals onto one another, hence is continuous in the maximal-ideal-adic topologies. It is the stated substitution: truncating a series $F=\sum_E a_Es^E$ in total variable degree gives polynomials converging in the maximal-ideal-adic topology; continuity gives $e(F)=\sum_Ea_E(t')^E$. The same expansion verifies equivariance explicitly: $h(e(F))=\sum_Ea_E\prod_i\chi'_i(h)^{E_i}(t')^E=e(h(F))$, using continuity of the action, fixed coefficients, and Step 3. For $d=0$ these sums reduce to constants and $e$ is the identity on $C$; for $l=d$ Step 2 fixes every variable. Thus all claimed clauses, including the empty cases, hold.
